'''Stefan Bergman''' (5 May 1895 – 6 June 1977) was a [[Russian Poland|Poland]]-born American [[mathematician]] whose primary work was in [[complex analysis]]. He is known for the [[positive-definite kernel|kernel function]] he discovered in 1922 at [[Humboldt University of Berlin|University of Berlin]].  This function is now known as the [[Bergman kernel]]. Bergman taught for many years at [[Stanford University]].<ref name="Gen">{{MathGenealogy|id=13649}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Born in [[Częstochowa]], [[Congress Poland]], [[Russian Empire]], to a German Jewish family,{{Sfnm|1a1=O'Connor|1a2=Robertson|1loc=[http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Bergman.html Stefan Bergman]}} Bergman received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] at University of Berlin in 1921, for a [[thesis|dissertation]] on [[Fourier analysis]]. His advisor, [[Richard von Mises]], had a strong influence on him, lasting for the rest of his career.<ref name="Bio">{{MacTutor Biography|id=Bergman}}.</ref> In 1933, Bergman was forced to leave his post at the Berlin University because he was a [[Jews|Jew]]. He fled first to [[Russia]], where he stayed until 1939, and then to [[Paris]]. In 1939, he emigrated to the [[United States]], where he would remain for the rest of life.<ref name="Bio"/> He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1951.<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780–2010: Chapter B|url=https://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterB.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=June 16, 2011}}</ref> He was a professor at Stanford University from 1952 until his retirement in 1972.<ref>[https://searchworks.stanford.edu/view/4085609 Stefan Bergman papers, circa 1940–1972 in SearchWorks, Stanford University Libraries]</ref> He was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1950 in Cambridge, Massachusetts<ref>Bergman, Stefan. [http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1950.1/Main/icm1950.1.0363.0373.ocr.pdf "On visualization of domains in the theory of functions of two complex variables."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161003175531/http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM1950.1/Main/icm1950.1.0363.0373.ocr.pdf |date=2016-10-03 }} In Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, vol. 1, pp. 363–373. 1950.</ref> and in 1962 in [[Stockholm]] (''On meromorphic functions of several complex variables'').<ref>Bergman, S. "On meromorphic functions of several complex variables, Abstract of short communications." Internat. Congr. Math., Stockholm (1962): 63.</ref> He died in [[Palo Alto, California]], aged 82.

===  Bergman Prize ===
The [[Stefan Bergman Prize]] in mathematics was initiated by Bergman's wife in her will, in memory of her husband's work. The [[American Mathematical Society]] supports the prize and selects the committee of judges.<ref name="Prize">[http://www.ams.org/prizes/supported-prizes.html Other Prizes and Awards Supported by the AMS<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> The prize is awarded for:<ref name="Prize"/>

# the theory of the [[positive-definite kernel|kernel function]] and its applications in real and complex analysis; or
# function-theoretic methods in the theory of [[partial differential equation]]s of [[Elliptic operator|elliptic type]] with a special attention to Bergman's and  related operator methods.
